answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each newcomer to earn a harbor of trust through a slow, sequential work record: every identity starts with only tiny, low-value jobs, and each completed job, verified by a different peer, unlocks slightly larger work, like crossing a canyon one narrow bridge at a time rather than leaping it. A raven that tried to fake a thousand identities would have to repeat that slow climb for each one, since the record cannot be bought, copied, or run in parallel, so the cost of each extra fake grows while honest agents keep their earned standing.
